newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Botswana surprises with 1996/97 budget surplus.
newsitem.headline: Botswana surprises with 1996/97 budget surplus.

text.p: Botswana will record its 14th consecutive budget surplus in fiscal 1996/97 (April-March), despite initial projections of a deficit, thanks to windfall central bank profits, according to Bank of Botswana estimates.
Research director Jay Salkin said on Thursday latest estimates suggested the central bank would turn a profit of around 1.7 billion pula in 1996/97, sharply up from 1.051 billion in 1995/96.
The government had initially budgeted a contribution from the Bank of Botswana this year of only around 975 million pula.
"Our investments have performed well and the depreciation of the pula will obviously boost the results," Salkin said in an interview.

The pula has fallen more than 20 percent against the U.S. dollar since the beginning of the year as the authorities have tracked the course of the ailing South African rand, intervening in the foreign exchange market to push the currency down.
The government had originally forecast a budget deficit of 636 million pula for 1996/97, the first shortfall since 1982.
Salkin said it was not possible to give a precise forecast of this year's budget deficit given other variables in government revenue and expenditure.
Extra costs not forecast at the time of the budget earlier this year included funds required to compensate cattle farmers whose animals were slaughtered to control an outbreak of bovine pneumonia.
However, this would be offset by higher than budgeted revenues from the diamond industry, which is enjoying buoyant prices for its gem-quality stones this year, he said.
